anomalies.observed: On the FCC Peripherals sheet the PWM driver U2 (PCA9685PW) is strapped to I2C address 0x41 (its A0 address pin is pulled high, and the sheet carries the explicit note 'I2C address: 0x41'), while it sits on the I2C2 bus (SCL pin26 -> I2C2_SCL_FCC, SDA pin27 -> I2C2_SDA_FCC).
anomalies.expected: The design specification's component table states the PWM/servo driver is 'NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40'. The intended address is therefore 0x40, i.e. all A0-A5 address pins tied low.

evidence.quote: FCCPeripherals sheet, PWM Driver block: 'U2 PCA9685PW ... I2C address: 0x41'
Component Table (Hades): 'PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40'

anomalies.impact: The servo/PWM driver responds on a different I2C address than the intended design specifies. Firmware that initializes/commands the PCA9685 at the documented address 0x40 will not find the device at 0x41, so the 16-channel PWM/servo outputs would not be driven as intended.

parsed.summary: Most of the build matches the specification (dual STM32H753/STM32F405, MIC26903+LD39200 power stage, INA219 at 0x40, BMI088/IIS2MDCTR/MPRLS/TMP100/EEPROM addresses, the documented barometer RESET/EOC swap, 10 mOhm shunt, 15 uH inductor, 5 V feedback divider). The one clear numeric deviation from the intended design is the PCA9685 PWM driver, which the drawing straps/annotates to I2C address 0x41 whereas the specification's component table states 0x40.
